questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Vitrinite reflectance Ro% rank indicator: Ro < 0.5% is:
options: High-volatile bituminous coal with strong caking
Semi-anthracite of very low volatile matter
questions.solution: Lignite: Ro<0.5%. Sub-bit: 0.5-0.6%. Bituminous: 0.6-2.0%. Anthracite: >2.0%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ridge push and slab pull forces: which is dominant in plate motion?
options: Ridge push, from gravitational sliding of the elevated ridge flanks
Equal contribution of ridge push and slab pull at all plate margins
Mantle drag exerted by large-scale convective overturn beneath plates
questions.solution: Slab pull > ridge pull. Plates attached to subducting slabs move faster (Pacific).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The age of oceanic crust increases in which direction relative to a mid-ocean ridge?
options: Toward the crest of the spreading ridge
Uniformly at the same rate across all basins
In proportion to distance from the subduction zone
questions.solution: Seafloor spreading: new crust at ridge, older further away.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Fission track dating relies on spontaneous fission of ²³⁸U producing damage trails; in apatite, tracks anneal at about:
options: U-Pb method applied to uranium minerals of the host rock that is being studied in detail for its complete thermal history
K-Ar method applied to potassium feldspars of the same igneous body and its samples
C-14 method applied to organic material of recent origin in the overlying beds
Spontaneous fission of ²³⁸U → damage trails in crystal. Track length T-dependent. Apatite: annealing ~110°C
questions.solution: Fission track: thermochronometer. Apatite (AFT): ~60-120°C. Zircon (ZFT): ~200-300°C.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The radioactive gas radon, which can accumulate inside buildings, is ultimately derived from what source?
options: Emissions from cement and brick building materials
Radon present in ordinary outdoor atmospheric air
Residual radon dissolved in domestic water pipes
questions.solution: Radon: 222Rn from uranium decay in rocks/soil. Enters buildings through cracks. Second leading cause of lung cancer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In well logging, the resistivity tool measures formation resistivity, which helps distinguish between:
options: Formation density from gamma ray scattering used to estimate the total porosity of the bed
Formation resistivity (ohm-m). Water vs hydrocarbon (low vs high Rt). LWD, wireline
Spontaneous potential of the borehole for permeable zones and clay content
Compressional slowness for porosity and the identification of secondary porosity
questions.solution: Rt vs Rxo (invaded zone). Archie: Sw = (a·Rw)/(ϕ^m·Rt)^{1/n}. Deep (LLd) vs shallow (LLs).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Diagenetic quartz cement in sandstone increases with:
options: Rise in relative sea level during transgression
Rate of extensional faulting in the basin
questions.solution: Quartz cement: pressure solution and silica migration. Increases with T (>70°C). Major porosity destroyer in sandstones.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Carbonate grain types: ooids, peloids, bioclasts, intraclasts. Ooids form in:
options: Cold, deep oceanic water far below the carbonate compensation depth
Glacial meltwater streams carrying suspended carbonate silt into fjords
Warm, shallow, agitated marine water (high energy)
Shallow, calm lagoonal water with abundant algae and low salinity
questions.solution: Ooids: spherical, concentric layers. Form in warm, shallow, agitated water. Bahama Banks type.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Fault breccia, composed of angular rock fragments within a fault zone, characteristically forms in which setting?
questions.solution: Fault breccia: angular fragments in fault zone. Forms in brittle regime (< ~10 km depth). Cataclasite is finer-grained equivalent.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What texture results from early crystals accumulating and settling in a magma chamber, producing layering?
options: Glass formed by the quenching of a mafic melt on the sea floor
Late-stage crystals that grew interstitially between earlier minerals
Early crystals accumulated by settling in magma chamber. Layering
Quench texture produced by rapid undercooling of volcanic glass
questions.solution: Cumulates: bottom of magma chamber. Chromite layers in Bushveld Complex.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: At the Al₂SiO₅ triple point, approximately 500°C and 4 kbar, which three polymorphs coexist?
options: Andalusite is stable at high temperature while kyanite forms only at near-surface atmospheric conditions of pressure
Andalusite, kyanite, sillimanite. T ~500°C, P ~4 kbar. Kyanite: high P. Andalusite: low P. Sillimanite: high T
Only a single Al₂SiO₅ phase is stable across the entire P-T field of crustal metamorphism regardless of grade
Sillimanite is the high-pressure polymorph and kyanite the high-temperature one, so the two never coexist
questions.solution: Triple point: all three coexist. Ky → Sil at ~4 kbar, ~550°C. And → Sil at ~550°C, <4 kbar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geostatistical interpolation method fits a variogram and yields a best linear unbiased estimate of unknown values?
options: Geostatistical interpolation. Variogram model (spherical, exponential, Gaussian). BLUE estimate
Deterministic interpolation in which every sample point receives an equal weight regardless of distance from the target
Nearest-neighbour resampling that ignores all spatial autocorrelation between samples
Spline interpolation that smooths the surface without fitting any variogram model
questions.solution: Kriging: semivariogram γ(h). Nugget, sill, range. Ordinary kriging: local mean unknown.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a barrier island facies model, the components include barrier, inlet, lagoon, and tidal delta, and the system is either:
options: Only beach and aeolian dune deposits with no other subenvironments
Only deep marine turbidites deposited on the continental rise and the abyssal plain, far from any shoreline
Aeolian desert dunes exclusively, with no marine influence at all
Barrier (beach, dune), inlet, lagoon, tidal delta. Transgressive (retreating) or regressive (prograding)
questions.solution: Barrier island: mixed-energy coast. Washover fan: overwash during storms. Inlet migration.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The metamorphic mineral staurolite crystallizes in which crystal system?
questions.solution: Staurolite — cruciform twins. Index mineral for medium-grade metamorphism.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A porphyritic texture (large crystals in a fine groundmass) indicates:
options: High-grade metamorphism with intense deformation of pre-existing crystals
Two stages of cooling — slow then fast
Deposition of sediment in a calm deep-water environment
Uniform rapid cooling of the entire magma body at the surface
questions.solution: Early slow cooling grows phenocrysts; later rapid cooling forms the fine matrix.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: As coal rank increases from lignite to anthracite, the volatile matter and moisture generally:
options: Stay constant throughout the coalification path
Increase together with the ash content
questions.solution: Higher rank means more fixed carbon and less moisture/volatiles, raising calorific value.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The chain of volcanoes formed as a lithospheric plate drifts over a stationary mantle plume is a hotspot track. It is best used to determine:
options: Linear age progression — plume track. Hawaii-Emperor bend (~47 Ma). Plate motion direction change
Random distribution of volcanoes without any systematic age relationship across the entire island chains
Anomalously high heat flow confined to the ridge axis and transform faults only along the ocean floor
Curved volcanic trails formed by migration of the plates toward an advancing subduction zone
questions.solution: Hotspot: K-Ar/track ages of islands. Pacific plate motion direction change at 47 Ma.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Formation of a rift valley within continental lithosphere occurs at which type of plate boundary?
options: Convergent boundaries where one plate overrides another
Intraplate settings unrelated to plate boundary stresses
questions.solution: Continental rift: extension thins crust. East African Rift.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In ichnology, the trace fossil association of Skolithos, Cruziana, and Nereites is used to interpret what?
options: Body fossils. Skolithos, Cruziana and Nereites are preserved hard skeletal parts, not traces of organism behaviour
Fossil fuels. Skolithos, Cruziana and Nereites are coal and petroleum source horizons within sedimentary basins
Chemical fossils. Biomarker molecules extracted from beds bearing Skolithos, Cruziana and Nereites
Skolithos (vertical, shallow marine), Nereites (deep sea), Cruziana (shallow marine). Behavioral classification
questions.solution: Trace fossils: tracks, burrows, trails. Seilacher facies: changes with water depth. Zoophycos.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Ediacaran biota of the fossil record represents what stage in the evolution of life?
options: Earliest prokaryotic life before the Archean
First shell-bearing organisms of the Cambrian
Primitive land plants of the Silurian period
questions.solution: Ediacaran: soft-bodied organisms ~575-539 Ma. Dickinsonia, Kimberella. Precambrian, pre-Cambrian explosion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lindgren's classification of ore deposits is based on which scheme of temperature and depth?
options: The four classes all form at the same temperature and pressure, differing only in the gangue minerals they contain
Hypothermal (high T, deep), Mesothermal (medium T), Epithermal (low T, shallow), Telethermal (very low T)
Two temperature classes, hot and cold, separated by a single fixed boundary
Classification based solely on the color and hardness of the gangue minerals
questions.solution: Lindgren: based on T and depth. Hypo: cassiterite, W. Meso: Au-quartz. Epi: Ag-Au.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Oxygen isotope ratio in ice cores indicates:
options: Global sea level at the time of deposition
The salinity of the original ocean water only
The wind speed prevailing at the ice sheet surface
questions.solution: Ice core δ18O: more negative = colder. Direct record of past temperature. Greenland and Antarctic cores provide 800kyr record.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Slaty cleavage, a planar fabric in low-grade metamorphic rocks, forms perpendicular to what?
options: Curved fabric formed by rotation of grains during progressive shearing
Planar fabric in low-grade metamorphic rocks. Perpendicular to compression
Random orientation of grains showing no preferred mineral alignment at all
Compositional layering inherited directly from original sedimentary bedding planes
questions.solution: Slaty cleavage: aligned micas. Rock splits along cleavage. Axial planar to folds.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral specimen of mass 105 g has a volume of 30 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
questions.solution: SG = mass/volume = 105/30 = 3.5.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Igneous rocks are formed primarily by which process acting on molten material?
options: Precipitation of salts as seawater evaporates in arid pans
Compaction and cementation of transported rock fragments
Cooling and solidification of magma or lava
Recrystallization of pre-existing rocks in the solid state
questions.solution: Igneous rocks crystallize from molten material (magma below ground, lava above).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Kimberlite pipe indicators for diamond exploration:
options: Indicator minerals such as G3G4 garnet and chromite
Magnetic anomalies recorded directly over the pipe with no other geochemical data
Presence of alluvial gold in stream sediments draining the pipe area
High radioactivity of the host rock measured by airborne radiometric surveying
questions.solution: Indicator minerals: Cr-pyrope garnet, chrome diopside, chromite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age, nature, and mineralisation of the Aravalli Supergroup of Rajasthan?
options: Mesozoic coal-bearing rift sequence with abundant plant fossils of Glossopteris
Archean (3.4-3.0 Ga) gneissic basement with tonalite-trondhjemite composition
Paleoproterozoic. Metamorphosed volcano-sedimentary sequence. Pb-Zn at Zawar
Cenozoic molasse basin fill of the Himalayan foredeep with thick alluvium
questions.solution: Aravalli: 2.2-1.8 Ga. Unconformably overlies Banded Gneissic Complex. UPb dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In Davis's cycle of erosion, what is the correct progression of a landscape from uplift through maturity to old age?
options: Landscape development follows no cycle of any kind at all in any region
Youth → Maturity → Old age. Uplift → rapid incision → graded → peneplain
Landscapes develop from old age back to renewed tectonic uplift at the end of the erosion cycle
Base level fall drives the landscape from the youthful stage through to old age
questions.solution: Davis: time-dependent. Peneplain: low relief, near base level. Rejuvenation by uplift.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a shear zone, and which features typically characterize ductile deformation within it?
options: A brittle fracture surface with distinct displacement and no deformed rock volume
Zone of ductile deformation. Mylonite, S-C fabrics, shear sense indicators
A zone of pure folding where no fabric or mylonite is ever developed
An undeformed region that is completely unaffected by the adjacent faulting
questions.solution: Shear zones: Porphyroclasts (σ, δ), mica fish. Sense: S-C fabrics indicate shear direction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Gutenberg discontinuity corresponds to the core-mantle boundary located at approximately what depth?
options: 410 km. The olivine to wadsleyite phase transition in the mantle
660 km. The ringwoodite breakdown to perovskite and magnesiowüstite
Surface. The boundary between the base of the crust and the upper mantle
questions.solution: CMB: Vp drops from 13.7 to 8.1 km/s. S-wave shadow zone. Liquid outer core.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Bouguer slab correction formula: 2*pi*G*rho*h
options: 0.0419*rho*h mGal with h in feet and rho in kg/m3
Approximately 0.0419*rho*h mGal (h in meters, rho in g/cm3)
2*pi*rho*h mGal assuming G is negligible at the Earth's surface
0.419*rho*h microGal with h in meters and density in g/cm3
questions.solution: Correction = 2*pi*G*rho*h. G=6.67e-11. For rho=2.67, h=100m: ~11.2 mGal.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which cratons constitute the Archean framework of Indian stratigraphy and their ages?
options: Himalayan collision zone with its thrust sheets and foreland basin deposits
Dharwar Craton (3.4-2.5 Ga), Singhbhum, Bastar, Bundelkhand
Deccan Trap basalts that cover about 500,000 square km of the western craton
Gondwana coal measures confined to the rift valleys of peninsular India
questions.solution: Dharwar: Sargur (older) and Dharwar Supergroup (younger). Greenstone belts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes syenite, which has <5% quartz and >90% alkali feldspar?
options: Granite containing more than fifty percent quartz by modal volume
A rock without feldspar in which mafic minerals dominate the mode
Syenite containing more than twenty percent modal quartz and no feldspar
questions.solution: Syenite: low quartz. Granite: >20% quartz. Both are felsic plutonic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Dynamic compaction: heavy weight (10-40t) dropped from 10-30m. Effective depth approximately:
options: √(WH) meters (W in tons, H in meters)
D = W/H meters where W is weight in tons and H is height
D = W×H meters with no dependence on the drop energy
D = (W+H)/2 meters for all ground conditions
questions.solution: Effective depth ≈ 0.5-0.8√(WH). For 20t from 20m: d ≈ 0.6×20 = 12m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rock mass rating (RMR): RMR = UCS+RQD+spacing+condition+groundwater. For granite with UCS=120MPa, RQD=80%, spacing=1m:
questions.solution: UCS=120→12, RQD=80→18, spacing=1m→20, condition→20, GW→15. Total ~85. Depends on exact ratings.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following techniques is used to improve weak ground for construction?
options: Only surface compaction of the topsoil using smooth wheel rollers and vibrating tampers
Compaction, grouting, soil nailing, stone columns, deep mixing, wick drains
Only removal and complete replacement of the weak soil mass beneath
Only increasing the moisture content of the foundation soil before loading
questions.solution: Ground improvement: increase strength, reduce settlement, improve liquefaction resistance.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What causes swelling ground in tunnels, and what support component is required?
options: Expansive minerals (smectite) → volume increase. Invert slab required
Sudden collapse of the roof with violent ejection of rock blocks into the heading
Continuous inflow of warm gas and water into the tunnel heading
Brittle bursting of the tunnel walls under very high stress
questions.solution: Swelling: reaction with water. Anhydrite → gypsum expansion. Montmorillonite in clay.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following is a recognized type of retaining wall?
options: Only masonry gravity walls built of stone masonry and cement mortar with no reinforcement
Gravity, cantilever, counterfort, anchored, soldier pile, sheet pile, diaphragm wall
Only rock-filled gabion walls placed along the toe of the slope to support it
Only precast concrete panels that are not connected to any foundation
questions.solution: Retaining wall: resist lateral earth pressure. Drainage critical. Tieback anchors.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Adakites show high Sr/Y and La/Yb; from what source do they form?
options: Partial melting of lower continental crust thickened by collision
Melting of the hydrated mantle wedge above a subduction zone
Melting of mid-ocean ridge basalt at a spreading centre
questions.solution: Adakite: slab melt signature. High Sr (plagioclase absent), high Y and Yb (garnet present).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sedimentary basins of India are referred to as Purana or Proterozoic basins?
options: The Himalayan foreland basins and the Siwalik molasse belt of the north
The Tethyan marine basins that bordered the southern margin of Tibet
The volcanic-plutonic basins filled with lava piles and batholithic granite
Cuddapah, Vindhyan, Delhi, Aravalli, Chattisgarh, Kaladgi, Bhima, Penganga
questions.solution: Purana: 'ancient'. Stable shelf deposits. Mostly undeformed except Delhi fold belt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are ripple marks used to interpret current flow and identify the top of a sedimentary bed?
options: Asymmetric (current) or symmetric (oscillation wave). Top of bed indicator
Asymmetric folds formed by tectonic compression during orogeny, unrelated to current flow
Fault-generated lineations on bedding planes formed by seismic slip
Planar fractures along which no displacement has taken place in the rock
questions.solution: Ripple marks: preserved on bed surfaces. Crest orientation perpendicular to current.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does phyllite differ from schist in terms of grain size and fabric appearance?
options: Phyllite: coarse-grained. Schist: fine-grained with silky sheen
Both are identical fine-grained rocks with the same foliation
Phyllite: melts completely. Schist: recrystallizes entirely in the solid state
Phyllite: fine-grained, silky sheen. Schist: coarse-grained, visible mica
questions.solution: Phyllite: gradational between slate and schist. Schist: foliated, >50% platy minerals.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the seismic reflection method, subsurface structure is imaged using which waves and processing steps such as CMP stacking and migration?
options: Mapping of the subsurface using critically refracted first arrivals at long offsets
Determination of the water table using direct current injected through steel electrodes
Estimation of rock density contrasts from measurement of the Earth's gravity field at the surface
Subsurface imaging by reflected P-waves. CMP stacking, migration. Resolution: λ/4 (~20m at 50 Hz)
questions.solution: Reflection: petroleum exploration. 2D, 3D seismic. Vibroseis (land), airgun (marine).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In an ore, the valueless minerals associated with the ore mineral are called:
questions.solution: Gangue is the commercially worthless material that must be separated from the ore mineral.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Luminescence dating (OSL, TL) of quartz and feldspar determines the burial age of sediment based on the last exposure to:
options: Burial age of sediment. Light-sensitive trapped charge in quartz/feldspar. Last exposure to sunlight
K-Ar method applied to volcanic minerals of the ash layers in the sedimentary section, giving crystallization ages
U-Pb method applied to detrital zircon grains from the same sedimentary sequence
Radiocarbon method applied to charcoal fragments from the same archaeological deposit
questions.solution: OSL: optical stimulated. TL: thermal. Range: few years to ~500 ka. SAR protocol.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a buttress unconformity, how do younger strata onlap against an older topographic high in a sedimentary basin?
options: Horizontal strata cut by a listric fault and repeated by compressional folding
Sedimentary beds eroded before the intrusion of a discordant igneous body
Strata onlap against topographic high (older rock). In sedimentary basins
A break where tilted strata are truncated below horizontal younger sedimentary beds
questions.solution: Buttress: onlap onto pre-existing relief. Common in basin margins. Progressive onlap.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A 6 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.6. The mineable reserve is about:
questions.solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×6×1.4×0.6 ≈ 30.2 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Saltwater-freshwater interface: Ghyben-Herzberg relation:
options: z = 20h giving an interface depth half of the Ghyben-Herzberg value
z = h giving an interface depth equal to the freshwater head value
z = (ρ_f/(ρ_s-ρ_f))·h ≈ 40h for h above sea level
z = 80h giving an interface depth twice the Ghyben-Herzberg value

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does X-ray diffraction identify clay minerals using glycol treatment and potassium saturation?
options: Ethylene glycol treatment expands smectite. K-saturation collapses vermiculite
No treatment is required because all clay minerals give unique and distinctive XRD patterns
Heat treatment alone destroys the 7Å peak of all smectites
Acid treatment removes interlayer water from kaolinite only
questions.solution: Smectite: expands with glycol (d₀₀₁ 17Å). Illite: no change (10Å). Kaolinite: disappears with K-sat.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does angular, poorly sorted, gravity-deposited colluvium differ from rounded, well-sorted, water-deposited alluvium?
options: Alluvium is deposited by gravity at the foot of a slope rather than by flowing water in a river channel
Colluvium and alluvium are exactly the same type of sediment deposit in every single respect known to geologists today
Colluvium: gravity-deposited, angular, poorly sorted. Alluvium: water-deposited, rounded, sorted
Colluvium is deposited by flowing water in a river channel and becomes rounded in the process
questions.solution: Colluvium: talus, debris flow deposits. Alluvium: river deposits. Diagnostic features: sorting, rounding.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spaceborne sensor carries OLI and TIRS instruments and has a 16-day revisit and a 185 km swath?
options: Landsat 8: OLI (9 bands, 30m) + TIRS (2 thermal, 100m). 16-day revisit. 185km swath
Landsat 8: carries only a single panchromatic band at 15m, and has no thermal capability
Landsat 8: 36 spectral bands at 250m resolution, offering a daily revisit period
Landsat 8: 13 bands, 10m resolution, a 5-day revisit period and a 290km swath
questions.solution: Landsat: 1972-2023. OLI bands: coastal, blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2, pan (15m), cirrus.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What in-situ parameter is obtained from a pressuremeter test?
options: In-situ stress-strain behavior. Modulus, limit pressure, creep pressure
A laboratory test on undisturbed samples to measure Atterberg limits
A cone penetration test (CPT) measuring tip resistance and sleeve friction ratio
A vane shear test measuring only the undrained shear strength of clay
questions.solution: Pressuremeter: expandable probe in borehole. Ménard pressuremeter. P_0, P_f, P_l.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do fixed mantle upwellings, such as Hawaii and Yellowstone, produce in the volcanic record?
options: Volcanoes scattered at random positions with no systematic age progression along any chain or fixed mantle source
Fixed mantle upwellings. Hawaii, Yellowstone, Reunion, Iceland. Age progression of volcanism
Volcanism restricted to subduction zones where slabs are recycled
Volcanism occurring only along diverging and converging plate boundaries
questions.solution: Hotspot: stationary relative to moving plate. Track: seamount chain (Emperor-Hawaii).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does the principle of superposition state about the order of strata in undeformed successions?
options: Youngest strata at the bottom and the oldest strata at the top of the column
Strata preserved in the reverse order of their age in every normal sequence
In undeformed strata, oldest at bottom, youngest at top
Strata occurring in a random order with no age relation between successive layers
questions.solution: Steno's law. Basis of relative dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What conditions and features characterize a glauconitic condensed section in the stratigraphic record?
options: Rapid deposition associated with maximum regression and falling sea level
High sedimentation rate with abundant coarse terrigenous clastic input
Deposition at low sea level during forced regression, marked by subaerial exposure and soil formation at the sequence boundary
Maximum flooding surface. Very slow sedimentation. Rich in glauconite, phosphorite, organic matter
questions.solution: Condensed: starved shelf. MFS. Thin but time-rich. Key correlation surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphism is best defined as which change occurring to a rock in the solid state?
options: Solid-state change in rock due to T/P change. No melting
Weathering of rocks by chemical and physical surface processes
Complete melting of rock followed by crystallization from magma
Erosion and transport of rock fragments by wind and water
questions.solution: Metamorphism: new minerals + textures. Grade: low (zeolite) → high (granulite).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: At a station the S-wave arrives 10 s after the P-wave. Using ~8 km per second of S–P delay, the epicentral distance is about:
questions.solution: distance ≈ (S−P time) × 8 km/s = 10×8 = 80 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: SEDEX deposits, formed by exhalation on the seafloor in sedimentary basins, are typically rich in which metals?
options: Volcanic-hosted massive sulfide deposits erupted at mid-ocean ridge spreading centers on the deep seafloor
Alluvial placers enriched by gravity settling of heavy resistant mineral grains
Zn-Pb-Ag deposits in sedimentary basins. Exhalative on seafloor. Broken Hill, McArthur River
Magmatic segregation of chromite and PGE in layered ultramafic intrusions
questions.solution: SEDEX: laminated ore. Reducing basin. Also large tonnage. Bagalkot (India).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral has passed through 1 half-life of an isotope whose half-life is 4.5 (in the given time units). Its age is:
questions.solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 1×4.5 = 4.5.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A fracture in rock along which there is no appreciable displacement is a:
questions.solution: Joints are cracks without relative movement of the blocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+15) = 61%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Thiem equation for steady radial flow to a well in a confined aquifer uses two observation wells and gives Q as:
options: Q = 2πT/ln(r) using only a single observation point
Q = 2πK(h₂-h₁)/r measured at the pumping well radius
Q = πK(h₂-h₁) for flow between two concentric circles
questions.solution: Thiem: equilibrium. Assumptions: homogeneous, isotropic, fully penetrating, steady state.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly defines drainage density and states the conditions under which it becomes high?
options: The total stream length multiplied by the area of the drainage basin that it drains
The number of streams in a drainage basin divided by the total drainage area of that basin in square kilometres
The drainage basin area divided by the total length of the main stream channel
Total stream length / basin area. High Dd = impermeable rock, high relief, low infiltration
questions.solution: Dd < 5 km/km² (coarse) to > 500 (fine). Lithology and climate control.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What engineering hazard is associated with limestone foundations?
options: Insoluble rock that never develops any cavities or sinkholes under any conditions
Good aggregate. Karst cavities → foundation hazard. Soluble in water
Always strong rock suitable for foundations in every terrain
Rock with no cavities and total resistance to all groundwater
questions.solution: Limestone: karst terrain. Sinkholes, caverns. Site investigation critical before construction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The principle of original horizontality states that sediments are originally deposited:
options: Along fault planes and within the fractures of the underlying basement rocks
In random orientations that bear no relation to the Earth's gravitational field
In vertical sheets resting against steep canyon and mountain escarpments
questions.solution: Tilted/folded strata indicate later deformation, since beds start horizontal.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Marble, a decorative building stone, is the metamorphic product of which parent rock?
options: Metamorphosed sandstone composed almost entirely of quartz grains
Volcanic rock rich in silica, alumina and iron oxide components
Sedimentary rock made up of interlocking calcite and dolomite cement
questions.solution: Marble: coarse, interlocking calcite. Pure white (Carrara). Impurities → colors.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A nonconformity is an unconformity in which sedimentary rocks overlie:
options: Tilted older sedimentary strata that dip at a high angle
A flat-lying sequence of strata with no break in deposition
Volcanic flows that have been folded into large open structures
questions.solution: A nonconformity has stratified rocks resting on eroded crystalline basement; an angular unconformity has tilted strata below.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which silicate structural group does the mineral augite belong?
questions.solution: Pyroxene: single chain, 90° cleavage. Augite: common in basalt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the role of secondary grout holes relative to primary ones?
options: Primary: initial spacing. Secondary: fill between primaries. Tertiary if needed
Secondary holes are always omitted from any grouting programme altogether
Secondary holes are drilled exactly at the same positions as the primary holes are placed
Primary holes are drilled last after the secondary holes are grouted
questions.solution: Split spacing grouting: primary holes → check coverage → secondary → tertiary.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Retrograde metamorphism during cooling or exhumation is characteristically marked by which reactions?
options: Prograde metamorphism that occurs during peak temperature and pressure conditions of the orogenic cycle
No change in the mineral assemblage during the entire metamorphic cycle at any stage
Dehydration reactions that release water during progressive burial and heating
Re-equilibration during cooling/exhumation. Hydration reactions (chlorite after garnet)
questions.solution: Retrograde: hydration, often incomplete. Greenschist overprint on amphibolite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In loess-paleosol sequences, which deposit records a glacial period and which records an interglacial, and why are they climate proxies?
options: Loess layers accumulate during the warm wet interglacial periods of the Quaternary
Loess and paleosol layers both have exactly the same origin and the same meaning in the stratigraphic record
Paleosol layers form during the cold dry glacial periods of the Quaternary
Loess = glacial period (cold, dry). Paleosol = interglacial (warm, wet). Climate proxy
questions.solution: Loess: wind-blown silt. Paleosol: weathered layer. China Loess Plateau: 2.6Ma record.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which subdivisions, from Ta to Te, make up the complete Bouma sequence of a turbidite?
options: Ta (massive/graded) → Tb (parallel laminated) → Tc (cross-laminated) → Td (laminated silt) → Te (pelagic mud)
Tb → Ta → Tc → Td → Te: parallel lamination first, then graded massive division
Ta → Tc → Tb → Td → Te: a graded massive division followed by cross-lamination, then parallel lamination and pelagic mud
Te → Td → Tc → Tb → Ta: pelagic mud at the base, grading upward to massive sand
questions.solution: Bouma: turbidite sequence. Ta: graded. Tb: plane parallel. Tc: ripples. Td: laminated. Te: pelagic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Cover subsidence, cover collapse, sinkholes, uvalas and poljes are all forms of which process in karst terrain?
options: Karst regions never experience any form of subsidence at all
Subsidence in karst regions involves only landsliding of the slopes
Subsidence in karst involves only riverbank erosion along the streams
Cover subsidence, cover collapse, sinkhole, uvala, polje
questions.solution: Cover collapse: sudden. Cover subsidence: gradual. Sinkhole: dissolution at surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 50% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
questions.solution: CV ≈ 70 × 50 = 3500 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Coal bed methane (CBM) desorption isotherm:
options: Henry's law for dissolved gas in the seam water
Fick's law of diffusion through the coal matrix
Darcy's law governing flow through cleat systems
questions.solution: Langmuir: adsorption on surface. V_L = maximum gas. P_L = pressure at half V_L.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock body that can store and transmit usable amounts of groundwater is a(n):
questions.solution: An aquifer is porous and permeable enough to yield water to wells.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 10 m over a horizontal distance of 20 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(10/20) ≈ 26.6°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Columnar (polygonal) joints in lava flows such as basalt result mainly from which process?
options: Planar fractures in sandstone formed by regional compressional stress
Curved sheet joints developed parallel to the topographic surface
Regular rectangular joint blocks formed in granite by unloading at depth
Polygonal columns in lava flows (cooling contraction). Basalt
questions.solution: Columnar: perpendicular to cooling surface. Giant's Causeway, Devil's Tower.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Serpentine is typically formed by the hydrothermal alteration of which parent mineral?
options: A primary mineral that crystallizes early from a basaltic magma at high temperature
Hard mineral with perfect cubic cleavage and high relief
Mg3Si2O5(OH)4. Alteration of olivine. Asbestos (chrysotile). Slippery surface
Framework silicate with no cleavage and conchoidal fracture
questions.solution: Serpentine: hydrous Mg silicate. Serpentinite: rock. Lizardite, antigorite, chrysotile.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Infiltration capacity is defined as the maximum rate at which water can enter the soil, and it is controlled by:
options: The rate at which water enters the soil surface and always exceeds the intensity of the rainfall received
Infiltration of water into the soil that is always greater than the hydraulic conductivity value of the soil formation
Maximum rate at which water enters soil. Controlled by rainfall intensity vs soil conductivity
A constant rate of entry of water into the soil that never changes with time at any stage
questions.solution: Horton: f = f_c + (f_0 - f_c)e^(-kt). Decays to f_c (saturated conductivity).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A 4 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.6. The mineable reserve is about:
questions.solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×4×1.4×0.6 ≈ 20.2 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a fault scarp, and how does erosion modify it over time?
options: Fault scarp: topographic expression of fault. Degraded by erosion
A topographic high that is always freshly exposed and never modified by erosion
A subsurface structure that has no expression at the ground surface at all
An erosional feature formed by rivers with no connection to fault movement
questions.solution: Fault scarp: free face. Triangular facets along normal fault range fronts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What streak colour does the mineral galena produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
questions.solution: Galena (PbS) — metallic grey, cubic cleavage. Main lead ore.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 45° shows a width of 30 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 30×sin45° ≈ 21.21 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a ductile shear zone, what do S-foliation and C-foliation represent, and what does their mutual angle indicate?
options: S-foliation (flattening), C-foliation (shear). Angle indicates shear sense
S-foliation is parallel to the shear zone boundary and C-foliation lies at 45° to it
Both S and C foliations are always perpendicular to each other at a fixed right angle
The angle between S and C fabrics remains constant and carries no shear-sense information
questions.solution: S-C: S (45° to shear), C (parallel). Type I (S-C mylonites). Type II (S-C' in S-C mylonites).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A slug test involves an instantaneous change in water level and is most suitable for:
options: Pumping at a constant rate for several continuous days at the pumping well site
A long term test of the aquifer that lasts for many months of continuous pumping
Instantaneous change in water level. For low K aquifers. Hvorslev, Bouwer-Rice
Steady pumping to equilibrium flow conditions in an observation well of the aquifer under test
questions.solution: Slug test: quick, inexpensive. T estimate for monitoring wells. Near-well conditions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Compared with surface (opencast) mining, underground coal mining is generally chosen when the seam is:
options: Deep, so that the stripping ratio becomes uneconomic
Shallow, so that stripping the overburden is cheap and easy
Always, regardless of seam depth or stripping ratio
Very shallow and thick so that opencast extraction is impractical
questions.solution: When overburden-to-coal (stripping) ratio is too high for opencast, underground methods become economic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In ophiolites, chromite occurs in which form and in which part of the mantle sequence?
options: Chromitite bodies forming only within stratiform layered intrusions, never in the mantle sections of ophiolites
Chromite concentrated only by residual lateritic weathering of peridotite outcrops
Podiform: mantle section. Stratiform: layered intrusion. Cr/(Cr+Al) indicates tectonic setting
Chromite composition giving no indication of the tectonic setting of formation
questions.solution: Podiform: mantle, harzburgite host. Stratiform: layered mafic intrusion. Cr#: higher = more depleted mantle.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the process and product of spheroidal weathering of jointed rocks?
options: Cracking caused only by repeated heating and cooling of the rock surface
Mechanical disintegration of the rock without any chemical alteration of minerals
Chemical dissolution confined strictly to open joints and fractures
Corners of joint blocks rounded by chemical attack. Concentric shells
questions.solution: Spheroidal: in jointed rocks. Water penetrates joints, attacks from all sides. Corestones.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS-based hydrological modeling, what processing of a DEM is required to derive flow accumulation, stream networks, and watersheds?
options: Flow accumulation and watershed delineation can be run on an unfilled DEM directly
Stream network extraction requires only slope; sink filling is optional preprocessing
Flow accumulation, stream network, watershed delineation. Sink filling required
Watershed boundaries are derived from aspect alone, without flow direction grids
questions.solution: DEM → fill sinks → flow direction (D8) → flow accumulation → stream threshold → watershed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Assimilation and fractional crystallization (AFC):
options: Mixing of two coeval mantle-derived magmas within a single chamber
Pure fractional crystallization of a single parental magma with no interaction with the wall rocks
Wholesale melting of the country rock with no crystallization taking place
Country rock assimilation + fractional crystallization. Combined effect. DePaolo equations
questions.solution: AFC: r = assimilation rate / crystallization rate. Trace element + isotope modeling.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the purpose of a Geotechnical Baseline Report (GBR)?
options: A legal document used only to sue the contractor after completion
A construction method statement prepared by the main contractor
Defines baseline ground conditions for contractual purposes
An optional report that is never used in contract administration
questions.solution: GBR: contractual baseline. Used in dispute resolution. FIDIC conditions of contract.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Division B of the Bouma sequence of a turbidite bed consists of which structure?
options: Upper structureless pelagic mudstone division E
questions.solution: Bouma B: upper parallel lamination. Upper flow regime. Graded bedding often present. Part of complete turbidite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What streak colour does the mineral magnetite produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
questions.solution: Magnetite (Fe3O4) — strongly magnetic. Black streak. Important iron ore.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Birefringence of a mineral viewed under a microscope is defined as what?
options: Reflection of light from a mineral surface back to the eye
Degree to which a mineral absorbs light of a given wavelength
Product of refractive index and specific gravity of the mineral
questions.solution: Birefringence: n_epsilon - n_omega. Measured on universal stage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes landfill leachate and the chemical constituents it carries?
options: Only suspended plastic debris and macro-scale litter
Only clean groundwater free of any dissolved metals
Only airborne dust particles carried by surface winds
questions.solution: Leachate: water percolating through waste picks up contaminants. Requires liner and collection system. Contaminates groundwater.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the hardness value of talc on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.solution: Talc (Mg3Si4O10(OH)2) — softest mineral. Diamond = 10.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: GPS (Global Positioning System): minimum 4 satellites for:
options: 3D position (x,y,z) without any receiver clock correction
2D position and elevation estimated from the same signals
Precise time only, position is determined by a single satellite
questions.solution: 4 satellites: solve for 4 unknowns (x,y,z,dt). More satellites improve geometry (DOP).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lineation in metamorphic rocks indicates:
options: Trace of the axial plane of a fold
Dip direction of the dominant fault plane
questions.solution: Stretching lineation: alignment of elongate minerals. Indicates transport/stretching direction. Key kinematic indicator.
